hints: Look closely at the table and ask yourself, in which stages do you actually see thick, condensed chromosomes made of two joined sister chromatids?
Remember sister chromatids stay joined together in prophase and metaphase, but separate in anaphase. Add those two stages together and divide by the total of 1000 cells.
walkthrough:
**Find the total number of cells**

First, let's get our whole sample size. Add up all the cells the student counted.

$$Total = 886 + 73 + 16 + 14 + 11 = 1000 \text{ cells}$$
This lovely total of 1000 will make our percentage very easy.

**Decide when chromosomes have two chromatids**

This is the key biology. After DNA replication, each chromosome is made of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere.

You only see them like this when chromosomes are condensed but not yet separated. That is prophase (73 cells) and metaphase (16 cells). In anaphase the sisters have pulled apart, in telophase they are single, and in interphase the DNA is loose chromatin, not visible chromosomes.

**Calculate the percentage**

Now add the correct cells and convert to a percentage.

$$Cells \text{ with two-chromatid chromosomes} = 73 + 16 = 89$$
$$Percentage = \frac{89}{1000} \times 100 = 8.9\%$$
That matches option B perfectly.

options.A: 7.3% is just prophase (73 out of 1000). It forgets metaphase, where chromosomes are still made of two chromatids lined up on the equator.
options.B: 8.9% is correct because prophase (73) plus metaphase (16) gives 89 cells out of 1000 with visible two-chromatid chromosomes.
options.C: 95.9% adds interphase (886) plus prophase (73). Interphase DNA has replicated but is uncondensed chromatin, not visible as two-chromatid chromosomes.
options.D: 97.5% adds interphase, prophase and metaphase. It incorrectly includes the 886 interphase cells where chromosomes are not visible in that form.
